task_37dbec84 — span-to-event lifecycle in s15_integrated_harness/trace_runtime.py (TraceRecorder):
1) L312-355 `span()` contextmanager: caller does `with recorder.span(start_event, end_event, data)`.
2) L334-336: allocates span_id via `new_id("span")` (counter under lock, L283-286) and reads enclosing parent span from the `_span_id` contextvar (defined L236-238).
3) L337-346: immediately emits the START event via `emit()`; its returned event_id becomes `start_id` for causal linking.
4) L347: pushes span onto context stack: `token = self._span_id.set(span_id)` — nested emits/spans inherit it as parent_span_id (L299-302).
5) L352: yields SpanHandle (L104-113); body runs; `SpanHandle.finish(**data)` (L112-113) merges caller data into `handle.end_data`.
6) L353-358: on exception, stamps `status="error"`, `error_type`, `error` into end_data, then RE-RAISES (not swallowed).
7) L359-361 `finally`: computes duration_ms from started_ns, defaults status="ok", resets `_span_id` token (restores parent).
8) L362-372: emits the END event (`handle.end_event`) carrying end_data, same span_id/parent_span_id, and `caused_by_event_id=start_id`.
9) L280-318 `emit()`: builds the JSONL record (schema_version, timestamp, monotonic_ns, elapsed_ms, run/turn/agent ids, thread info, data via safe_value); L317→L288-295 `_write()` appends + flushes line-buffered under `self._lock`.
Net: one span = start event + end event in JSONL, correlated by span_id and caused_by_event_id; nesting encoded via the contextvar stack.
